# Crate & Barrel CEO plans a 50-store expansion to win customers from rivals: ‘It’s absolutely a market steal play.’
November 27, 2026, 11:00 AM ET
![Facade with sign and logo at Crate and Barrel home decor retail store, Walnut Creek, California, August 25, 2025. (Photo by Smith Collection/Gado/Getty Images)](https://fortune.com/img-assets/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/GettyImages-2232220176.jpg?format=webp&w=1440&quality=75)
Facade with sign and logo at Crate and Barrel home decor retail store, Walnut Creek, California, August 25, 2025. (Photo by Smith Collection/Gado/Getty Images)
Few retail CEOs have had a more turbulent run than Janet Hayes. Since taking over Crate & Barrel in 2020, she has steered the furniture retailer through a pandemic and repeated tariff shocks. Now she’s betting the company can come out of it on the offensive.

“You don’t feel it until you’re being tested, but the global supply chain is fragile,” Hayes told *Fortune* in an interview at the new location of CB2, Crate & Barrel’s sister brand, in New York’s Chelsea district. “You can have the best-laid plans, you can map your ocean liners, you can decide what vendors you’re going to work with, but culture is everything to get through it.”

Crate & Barrel is part of privately held German retail group Otto Group, which does not publish financial results but did report earlier this year that Crate & Barrel revenue rose 1.6% last year. Given that the furniture market is stagnant in the U.S., Hayes says growth has to come at the expense of the competition. “It’s absolutely a market steal play,” says Hayes, who earlier in her career was a senior executive at [Williams-Sonoma](https://fortune.com/company/williams-sonoma/) and at [Nike](https://fortune.com/company/nike/). Hayes plans on adding 30 new Crate & Barrel and CB2 stores to its current count of 100 in the next three years, as well as 20 more in the two years after that.
